studies.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice.
evidence_quotes: we report here that rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age.
Expressed as mean lifespan, the effect sizes were 9% for males and 13% for females in the pooled dataset.

studies.title: The mTOR pathway is necessary for survival of mice with short telomeres.
evidence_quotes: 3-month-old wild type and second-generation telomerase-deﬁcient mice (G2 Terc−/−) in a C57BL/6 genetic background14 were fed with either control chow or chow- containing encapsulated rapamycin at 42 ppm (mg of drug per kg of food)31.

We found that rapamycin treatment increased median longevity of wild-type mice (Terc+/+) by 39%, resulting in a median longevity of 26.5 months in rapamycin-fed Terc+/+ mice compared to only 19 months in the control-fed cohorts (Fig. 1b).

studies.title: Long-lasting geroprotection from brief rapamycin treatment in early adulthood by persistently increased intestinal autophagy.
evidence_quotes: In mice, a 3-month, early treatment also induced a memory effect, with maintenance similar to chronic treatment, of lysozyme distribution, Man2B1 level in intestinal crypts, Paneth cell architecture and gut barrier function, even 6 months after rapamycin was withdrawn.
Rapamycin treatment started on day 30 extended lifespan (P = 2.13 × 10−6) to a lesser degree than did lifelong treatment (P = 1.04 × 10−13; Supplementary Table 2).

studies.title: Inhibition of S6K lowers age-related inflammation and increases lifespan through the endolysosomal system.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin treatment also elevated Syntaxin 12/13 levels in mouse liver and prevented age-related increase in noncanonical NF-κB signaling

Suppression of TORC1 signaling genetically or pharmacologically by the US Food and Drug Administration-licensed drug rapamycin (Rapa), promotes lifespan and healthspan in various model organisms including nema- tode worms, fruit flies and mice

studies.title: The geroprotectors trametinib and rapamycin combine additively to extend mouse healthspan and lifespan.
evidence_quotes: We measured the survival of mice on diets contain- ing only rapamycin (42 mg kg–1), the dose so far inducing the largest increase in longevity20, or both rapamycin (42 mg kg–1) and trametinib (1.44 mg kg–1).

intermittent rapamycin treatment extended lifespan in both sexes to a similar extent (P < 0.0001, log-rank test; P = 0.2481 for the sex–drug interaction, Cox proportional hazard) with an increase in median and maximum lifespan of 17.4% and 16.5%, respectively, in female mice (Fig. 2b) and 16.6% and 18.3%, respectively, in male mice (Fig. 2c).

studies.title: Cap-independent translation: A shared mechanism for lifespan extension by rapamycin, acarbose, and 17α-estradiol.
evidence_quotes: We collected livers and kidneys of young mice (6 months of age, Y), old mice (22 month of age, O), and mice treated with either ACA, Rapa, or 17aE2 from 6 to 22 months of age (O, Early) or from 18 to 22 months of age (O, Late).
Rapa inhibits the activity of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), leading at optimal doses to 20%–25% lifespan extension in male and female mice

studies.title: Drug-Based Lifespan Extension in Mice Strongly Affects Lipids Across Six Organs.
evidence_quotes: Drug treatments started at 4 months of age using UM‐HET3 mice and were administered with the food at 14.4 ppm (mg/kg food) for 17‐α estradiol (Steraloids, Newport, Rhode Island), 1000 ppm (mg/kg food) for acarbose (Spectrum Chemical Mfg. Corp., New Brunswick, New Jersey), 14 ppm (mg/kg food) for rapamycin (Emtora, San Antonio, Texas), and 180 ppm (mg/kg food) for canagliflozin (University of Michigan hospital pharmacy).

Using Jonckheere's trend test to associate increased average lifespans with metabolic changes for each sex, we found sexual dimorphism in metabolism of plasma, liver, gastrocnemius muscle, kidney, and inguinal fat.

studies.title: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has limited effects on aging.
evidence_quotes: we performed to determine whether rapamycin slows the rate of aging in male C57BL/6J mice.

Survival analysis applied to all treated cohorts, and lifespan extension by rapamycin was demonstrated relative to corresponding vehicle controls (Figure 1), confirming previously reported longevity effects (8–11).

studies.title: Health Effects of Long-Term Rapamycin Treatment: The Impact on Mouse Health of Enteric Rapamycin Treatment from Four Months of Age throughout Life.
evidence_quotes: At four months of age 160 mice, 80 animals per sex, began receiving mouse chow (Purina 5LG6) containing either microencapsulated rapamycin (14 ppm) or empty capsules (eudragit = control)
Consistent with our previous findings, survival of both males and females was modestly enhanced in YF animals [35].

evidence_quotes: treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin increased lifespan of Bmal1−/− mice by 50%

studies.title: p53 and rapamycin are additive.
evidence_quotes: Mice were fed chow containing empty Eudragit capsules (control) or capsules containing 14 ppm eRapa, the concentration previously shown to extend lifespan, delay tumor-related death, retard a number of age-related pathologies, and improve cerebral function
eRapa extended the median survival of p53+/- (520 to 582 days, p=0.0522) and p53+/+ mice (681 to 802.5 days, p=0.0013).

studies.title: Dose-dependent effects of mTOR inhibition on weight and mitochondrial disease in mice.
evidence_quotes: we compared the effects of dietary rapamycin at doses ranging from 14 to 378 PPM on developmental weight in control and Ndufs4 knockout mice and on health and survival in the Ndufs4 knockout model.

The highest oral dose, approximately 27-times the dose shown to extend murine lifespan, increased survival in Ndufs4 knockout mice similarly to daily rapamycin injection without observable adverse effects.

studies.title: Transient rapamycin treatment can increase lifespan and healthspan in middle-aged mice.
evidence_quotes: we set out to investigate whether a single three-month treatment regimen can extend lifespan and healthspan in C57BL/6JNia mice starting at 20–21 months of age.
After receiving the lower dose, both male and female mice lived about 50% longer than untreated mice, and showed improvements in their muscle strength and motor coordination.
